messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert (PD-84291) -> SEV2: runtime-prod GPU OOMs detected on model-redwood-7b-quant. 50+ OOMs in last 5m across pool runtime-gpu-prod-us-east-1. Link: https://pd.example/PD-84291 :rotating_light:

pagerduty: Paging sam (oncall)

sam (oncall): On it. Acknowledged PD-84291. Will triage and coordinate. Pls post any immediate mitigation ideas.

maya (runtime): Seeing repeated OOM traces in worker logs. Root cause unclear yet. Starting with pod-level nvml checks and recent deploy diffs.

kevin (sre): Any customer impact metrics? Error spikes?

emily (support): A few customers reported increased 500s for chat endpoints since ~09:02. Tickets 1234, 1236 mention failed responses and long tails. Not wide yet but growing.

sam (oncall): Timeline quick notes: alert fired ~09:02. First error visible in infra logs ~09:01:53.

maya (runtime): Pasting nvml snapshots and mem stats from node gpu-12 now:

```text
# nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,memory.total,memory.used,memory.free --format=csv
index, name, memory.total [MiB], memory.used [MiB], memory.free [MiB]
0, A100-40GB, 40960 MiB, 39120 MiB, 1840 MiB
1, A100-40GB, 40960 MiB, 39600 MiB, 1360 MiB
```

```text
# top processes using GPU memory (sample)
PID   USER   GPU_MEM
23541 red   15800 MiB  -> model-redwood-7b-quant worker
23562 red   15200 MiB  -> model-redwood-7b-quant worker
23600 red   12600 MiB  -> model-2b-variant
```

maya (runtime): Also saw frequent allocations failing with e.g. "CUDA out of memory trying to allocate 512MB" in logs.

jia (ml-infra): Two hypotheses off the bat: 1) KV cache growth across long-chat sessions not getting pruned and causing fragmentation across repeated sessions (we added larger per-user cache TTL in last rollout), 2) a change to the router batching heuristics increased batch_size to 8 for this model which pushes memory over on tail cases.

sam (oncall): Good. Can we test quick mitigation: reduce batch_size and temporarily disable kv cache for model-redwood-7b-quant?

maya (runtime): I can push a config change to reduce batch_size from 8 -> 4 for that model route and set kv_cache.enabled=false for the variant. Rolling change to canary first.

kevin (sre): Recommend also draining the busiest pod and restarting to defragment GPU memory. Scaling actions might not free fragmentation until restart.

sam (oncall): Go for it. Make sure canary targets a single node first. Post the exact commands/config you apply.

maya (runtime): Applying canary now. Patch snippet:

```yaml
# runtime router config (canary)
routes:
  - model: redwood-7b-quant
    batch_size: 4
    kv_cache:
      enabled: false
      ttl_seconds: 0
    rollout: 5% # canary
```

maya (runtime): Pushing patch -> kubectl apply -f canary-router-redwood7b.yaml

ops: deploy-bot: rollout started for router config canary (deployment/router-redwood-7b:canary).

maya (runtime): Canary applied. Observing first 60s of traffic.

jia (ml-infra): While that runs, quick check: we also recently increased max_sequence_length to 4096 for this model in commit abc123 — could lead to larger KV caching per request. If clients send long contexts + batch_size=8, memory multiplies.

emily (support): Noted — customer tickets mention longer sessions after new chat feature shipped yesterday. Might line up.

maya (runtime): Canary looks promising — no OOMs in the canary pod for the last 90s. CPU/latency stable. I'm scaling canary from 5% -> 30% to validate.

kevin (sre): Meanwhile I'll drain and restart the top 2 pods on node gpu-12 to free fragmentation. Drain + restart initiated.

ops: kube-bot: cordon+drain node gpu-12; restarting pod redwood-7b-quant-worker-23541.

maya (runtime): Pod restart completed. Post-restart memory usage looks clean, nvml shows more free memory.

```text
# after restart
index 0 free 12000 MiB
index 1 free 11000 MiB
```

sam (oncall): Customer impact update? emily?

emily (support): Error rate dropped back to baseline for most customers. Two tickets still show failures — likely edge cases. We'll follow up.

jia (ml-infra): Looks like both mitigations helped: lower batch size and disabling kv cache reduced sustained peak and the restart addressed fragmentation. Hypothesis: kv cache + high batch_size + occasional long sequences triggered the fragmentation/OOM cascade. Need to confirm with logs.

sam (oncall): Good. For in-incident RCA tracking: I'll create a living timeline and ask folks to paste relevant logs here. Action items: maya to collect pre/post nvml, jia to run reproducer with long contexts and batch_size=8, kevin to note restart nodes and timestamps, emily to map affected customers. I'll handoff to kevin at +30m.

maya (runtime): Attaching sample logs showing allocation failures (grep snippet):

```text
[2026-03-15T09:01:54Z] ERROR model-runner: allocation failed: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory trying to allocate 536870912 bytes
[2026-03-15T09:01:55Z] WARN kv-cache: cache size 2.1GB (per-session), sessions active: 34
[2026-03-15T09:01:56Z] ERROR runtime: failed to reserve tokens for batch id=xyz
```

jia (ml-infra): Running local repro with 64-token queries but long conversation history ~2500 tokens, batch_size=8. Observed OOM in ~3/10 runs and high fragmentation on profiler. Reproducer steps and snippet:

```bash
# reproduce: send 8 concurrent requests each with long prefix
for i in {1..8}; do 
  curl -s -X POST https://runtime/redwood-7b-quant/generate -d '{"prompt":"<long 2500-token history>","max_tokens":64}' &
done
```

jia (ml-infra): With kv_cache disabled and batch_size=4, reproducer runs cleanly.

sam (oncall): OK mitigations look effective. I'm going to mark incident as mitigated for customer-facing impact. Keeping thread open for RCA artifacts. Handoff: kevin you'll own next 30m and collect more logs/timeline?

kevin (sre): Ack. I'll run deeper memory fragmentation profiling and coordinate a permanent patch plan: revert TTL bump, add autopruning of per-session KV cache over threshold, and tune router batching by model/sequence length.

emily (support): I'll close the two high-touch tickets and send a note to affected customers: root cause was runtime KV cache + batching causing memory fragmentation and OOMs; we applied an emergency config to reduce batch size and disable kv-cache, restarted pods, and will follow up with a permanent fix.

sam (oncall): Nice work. Before I handoff, small checklist: 1) collect scheduler traces, 2) gather nvml dumps pre/post (maya), 3) reproduce logs and attach heap profiles (jia), 4) list affected customers and severity (emily). Post those here and we'll assemble an in-thread timeline for RCA.

maya (runtime): Uploading nvml dumps and scheduler traces to incident artifact storage: s3://redwood-incidents/PD-84291/nvml/ and s3://redwood-incidents/PD-84291/traces/

jia (ml-infra): Uploaded reproducer results and profiler flamegraphs to s3://redwood-incidents/PD-84291/repro/

kevin (sre): Taking over monitoring and post-incident tasks. Will draft mitigation plan and RFC for permanent changes: smarter batch sizing based on avg seq length, kv cache autoshrink, and enforced pod restarts during reconfigs to avoid fragmentation.

sam (oncall): Handing off. Logged as handoff in PagerDuty. Thanks all.

incident-bot: Incident PD-84291 status -> mitigated (customer-facing) by sam (oncall) -> handoff to kevin (sre).

kevin (sre): I'll keep this thread as the single source for RCA artifacts. Please add any remaining logs. We'll close when the RFC and timeline are ready. :thumbsup:
